overall_analysis.summary: The overall difficulty distribution is severely skewed toward the lower-middle range. 48.3% of all MCQ items are Moderate (vs 30% target), while only 3.3% are Difficult (vs 25% target) and zero items are Very Difficult (vs 10% target). The Easy and Moderate-Easy bands are moderately overweight, but the primary defect is the near-total absence of higher-difficulty items.

certified_pool_analysis.methodology: Estimated proportionally per-pack (assuming difficulty distribution within each pack is roughly proportional between certified and non-certified items)
certified_pool_analysis.learner_impact_summary: The certified (learner-facing) pool of 2,298 items carries nearly identical difficulty skew as the full pool. Learners experience: (1) ~47.6% of tested questions at Moderate difficulty — 17.6pp above the CAQS target, creating a perception of a 'flat' exam with insufficient cognitive challenge; (2) only ~3.4% at Difficult level — learners are not being prepared for the upper cognitive tiers present in the actual CMA exam; (3) zero Very Difficult items — the top difficulty tier is completely absent from the learner experience.

comparison_to_mcq.difficult_gap: Case studies have 10.7x more Difficult items than MCQ pool proportionally (35.7% vs 3.3%)
comparison_to_mcq.easy_gap: Case studies have 23x fewer Easy items proportionally (0.9% vs 21.1%)
comparison_to_mcq.combined_pool_calibration: When case studies and MCQs are combined (3,285 items), the Difficult band would be (266+85)/(745+2540) = 351/3285 = 10.7% — still well below the 25% target but substantially better than the MCQ-only 3.3%
comparison_to_mcq.note: Case studies may be a source of 'recalibration templates' — items currently labeled Difficult that could inform what a well-calibrated Difficult MCQ looks like

remediation_magnitude.realistic_approach: Given zero Very Difficult items exist, full 10% target is infeasible through recalibration alone.
